# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 68 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 68 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_068_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 6, Part 6 — Why God Allows Suffering; The Reward of Endurance

**68:1** "Lord," I said, "I also want to understand why the Lord doesn't simply protect his servants from the troubles and hardships of this life — why he allows them to go through these things." "He can't protect them from it," he said. "They have to go through all these things. The Lord has appointed these afflictions to test those he has designed for testing."

**68:2** "But why are some tested with a little and others with a lot?" "Because not everyone is equally capable of enduring," he said. "Some have weak faith and others have strong faith. Those with strong faith have to bear heavier trials so that they can be brought to full maturity. Those with weaker faith get lighter trials so they aren't completely crushed."

**68:3** "The Lord keeps close watch over everyone who is suffering and will eventually pay each person back according to what they have done. After the full time has passed, the Lord will give everyone their wage." "But will there be any mercy for those who suffer, lord?" I asked. "Yes," he said, "there will."

**68:4** "Those who suffer and endure their suffering without being overcome — without their spirit being broken — will receive immense glory from the Lord. But those who suffer and don't hold up — those whose spirit does break — they will receive none of that glory and will not live for God. The person who keeps the commandments and endures through the suffering will receive life and grow great in it."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing the testing-and-endurance theology of Hermas.*
